mainTopic: Why a childless marriage is not in the משנה's list of forced divorces; the disease ראתן; stories of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי חנינא בר פפא at their deaths; and the close of the perek.
overview: The גמרא explains why the משנה's list of forced divorces leaves out a marriage with no children. In the listed cases, even מוכה שחין, a wife who wants to stay can find a way, such as living with him under the watch of witnesses. In a childless marriage she cannot stay at all. A ברייתא from רבי יוסי then teaches that marital relations harm people with skin diseases, and those with ראתן most of all. The גמרא gives the cause of ראתן, its signs, and אביי's dramatic cure. It then tells how the חכמים kept far from people with ראתן, while רבי יהושע בן לוי sat with them and learned תורה, trusting it to protect him. This leads into the stories of how רבי יהושע בן לוי entered גן עדן alive and how רבי חנינא בר פפא tried the same trick. The perek הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ closes with why people in בבל did not get ראתן or צרעת, followed by the הדרן.

steps.title: Blemishes versus a childless marriage
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה's cases of blemishes, a wife who wants to stay is allowed to. In a marriage with no children, she is not allowed to stay, even if she wants to.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, if she says 'I want to be with him,' we leave her alone. Here, even if she says 'I want to be with him,' we do not leave her alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's list of forced divorces leaves out a marriage with no children. In the listed blemish cases the wife can choose to stay, but in the childless case she cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With blemishes, the only person who suffers is the wife, so she can give up her claim. In a childless marriage the husband is not keeping the מצוה of פריה ורביה. So the wife's agreement does not stop בית דין from forcing a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (the case of a marriage with no children)
I want to be with him
We leave her alone (we don't force a divorce)

phrases.english: There, when she says: 'I want to be with him' —
phrases.notes: 'There' means the blemishes listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: we leave her alone.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמְרָה ״הָוְיָנָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ״ —
phrases.english: Here, even though she says: 'I want to be with him' —
phrases.notes: 'Here' means a wife who has had no children with him.

phrases.english: we do not leave her alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כִּי אָמְרָה הָוְיָנָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ שָׁבְקִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous amud: why the משנה does not list the childless marriage among the forced divorces.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית דין also forces a divorce in a childless marriage, one would expect the משנה to list it together with the blemish cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the blemish cases her wish to stay is respected. In the childless case it is not.

steps.title: Challenge from the husband with boils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה itself has a case, מוכה שחין, where her wish to stay is not respected. So the claimed difference does not hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a man with boils? Even if she says 'I want to be with him,' we do not leave her alone. As the משנה says: 'except for one with boils, because it wears him away.' And it is taught in that same משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 1. The משנה's own list includes a case where the wife is not allowed to stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the childless case is missing from the משנה because there her wish to stay is ignored. But for מוכה שחין her wish is also ignored, because relations would harm him, and yet the משנה does list it. So that difference cannot be why the childless case was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A man suffering from boils (a serious skin disease)
That it wears away (rots) his flesh
And yet it is taught (in the same משנה)

phrases.english: But there is the man with boils,
where even though she says: 'I want to be with him' —
we do not leave her alone.
As we learned: except for a man with boils,
because it wears him away
and yet it is taught there!
phrases.notes: He means: and yet the משנה does list it, so your reason can't explain why the childless case was left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 1's answer that the משנה lists only cases where the wife's wish to stay is respected, and so leaves out the childless case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For מוכה שחין we also do not leave her alone, yet the משנה lists it. So 'her wish is ignored' cannot be the reason the childless case is missing from the list.

steps.title: Living together under the eye of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Even with מוכה שחין, she may stay married if she lives with him under the watch of witnesses. In the childless case, even that is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, if she says 'I will live with him in front of witnesses,' we leave her alone. Here, even if she says 'I will live with him in front of witnesses,' we do not leave her alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by sharpening the difference. With מוכה שחין she can still stay married in a careful way, but in the childless case she cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מוכה שחין the problem is only the danger of relations. So if witnesses make sure they are never alone together, she may stay his wife. In the childless case the whole problem is that no children are coming, so staying without relations does not help at all.
steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה's cases, even מוכה שחין, a wife may find a way to stay. In a marriage with no children, בית דין forces the divorce no matter what she says.

phrases.english: There, when she says: 'I will live with him with witnesses' —
phrases.notes: She means she'll stay his wife but never be alone with him, so there are no relations.

phrases.english: we leave her alone.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמְרָה ״דָּיְירָנָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ בְּסָהֲדֵי״ —
phrases.english: Here, even though she says: 'I will live with him with witnesses' —
we do not leave her alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כִּי אָמְרָה דָּיְירָנָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ בְּסָהֲדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוכה שחין seemed to have the same rule as the childless case: she is never allowed to stay.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every case the משנה lists, even מוכה שחין, leaves her some way to stay married (with witnesses). The childless case leaves no way at all, so it is not on the list.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's teaching about twenty-four skin diseases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: an elder from ירושלים told רבי יוסי there are 24 kinds of boil diseases. Relations harm all of them, and ראתן most of all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי said, an elder of ירושלים told me there are twenty-four kinds of people with boils. The חכמים said relations are harmful to all of them, and people with ראתן are harmed most of all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives more information about מוכה שחין. It explains that relations are dangerous for these sick people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up why the משנה forces a divorce for מוכה שחין: relations harm him. It also introduces the worst of these diseases, ראתן, which the גמרא will now discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: People afflicted with ראתן, a severe skin disease

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׂח לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: A certain elder from the people of Jerusalem told me:
There are twenty-four kinds of people with boils,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים תַּשְׁמִישׁ קָשֶׁה לָהֶן,
phrases.english: and about all of them the Sages said relations are harmful to them,
and for those with ra'atan it is harmful most of all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives background on the מוכה שחין mentioned in Steps 2-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations harm all 24 kinds of boil sufferers, and ראתן sufferers most of all.

steps.title: How does ראתן come about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what causes the disease ראתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what does it come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what causes ראתן? This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a request for information about the disease just mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: From what does it come about?

phrases.english: From what does it come about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ראתן mentioned in Step 4.

steps.title: Bloodletting before relations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if the man let blood and then had relations, the children are weak. If both let blood and then had relations, the children will have ראתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one who let blood and then had relations will have weak children. If both of them let blood and then had relations, he will have children with ראתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Relations right after bloodletting harm the children, and when both parents let blood, the children get ראתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. If only the man let blood, the children are weak. If both did, the result is worse: the children have ראתן.

phrases.english: As it was taught: one who let blood and had relations —
will have weak children.
If both of them let blood and had relations —
he will have children with ra'atan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ראתן comes from both parents letting blood and then having relations.

steps.title: רב פפא: only if he ate nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the ברייתא: the danger is only when nothing was eaten between bloodletting and relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: we said this only when he did not taste anything. But if he tasted something, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a limit to the ברייתא from Step 6. The danger exists only when no food was eaten in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounded like a blanket warning. רב פפא narrows it: eating something after bloodletting removes the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא טָעֵים מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: We said this only when he did not taste anything,
but if he tasted something —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger of relations after bloodletting applies only if nothing was eaten in between.

steps.title: What are the signs of ראתן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to recognize ראתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are its signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the symptoms of ראתן. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the cause, the גמרא now wants to know how to identify the disease.

phrases.english: What are its signs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the cause of ראתן to its symptoms.

steps.title: The symptoms of ראתן
steps.stepSummary: His eyes water, his nose runs, drool comes from his mouth, and flies rest on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His eyes drip, his nose runs, drool comes out of his mouth, and flies land on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists four signs of ראתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are outward signs anyone can see. That makes the disease easy to identify.

phrases.english: His eyes drip,
and his nostrils run,
and drool comes out of his mouth,
and flies rest upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Watering eyes, runny nose, drool, and flies resting on him.

steps.title: What is the cure for ראתן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ראתן is treated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is its cure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a cure for ראתן. אביי answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the medical discussion: first the cause, then the signs, and now the treatment.

phrases.english: And what is its cure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from symptoms to treatment.

steps.title: אביי's remedy for ראתן
steps.stepSummary: אביי lists ingredients to cook together, and says to bring the patient into a sealed marble house, or else a house with very thick brick walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: take pila, ladanum, ground nut shell, shavings of smoothed hides, kelil malka, and the calyx of a red date palm. Cook them together and bring him into a marble house. If there is no marble house, bring him into a house with walls seven bricks and a small brick thick.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the recipe for the cure and where to do the treatment. The rest of the procedure comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts: the mixture of six ingredients cooked together, and a closed room. A marble house is best. If none is available, a house with very thick walls is the backup.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Pila and ladanum,
phrases.notes: These are kinds of plants.

phrases.english: the ground shell of a nut,
and shavings of smoothed hides,
and kelil malka,
phrases.notes: Literally 'king's crown', the name of a plant.

phrases.english: and the calyx of a red date palm.
And he cooks them together,
and brings him into a marble house.
And if there is no marble house —

phrases.aramaic: מְעַיֵּיל לֵיהּ לְבֵיתָא דְּשַׁב לִבְנֵי וַאֲרִיחָא,
phrases.english: he brings him into a house of seven bricks and a small brick,
phrases.notes: He means the walls are that thick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10. The answer continues in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A cooked mixture of six ingredients, given in a sealed marble house or a thick-walled brick house.

steps.title: Finishing the treatment: removing the creature from the brain
steps.stepSummary: אביי's treatment continues. The mixture is poured on the head, the skull is opened, and the creature is removed with myrtle leaves and tweezers, then burned so it will not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He pours three hundred cups of the mixture on the patient's head until the skull softens, and opens it to the brain. He brings four myrtle leaves, lifts each foot of the creature, and puts a leaf under it. Then he takes it out with tweezers and burns it, because if he does not, it will come back to the patient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's answer from the last step about how ראתן is treated. These are the final steps of the procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 described the mixture and the sealed house. Here we learn what the mixture is for: it softens the skull so the creature on the brain can be reached. The leaves under its feet stop it from clinging as it is pulled out, and burning it keeps the illness from returning.

phrases.aramaic: וְנָטֵיל לֵיהּ תְּלָת מְאָה כָּסֵי עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ,
phrases.english: And he pours three hundred cups on his head,
phrases.notes: These are cups of the mixture אביי listed in the last step.

phrases.english: until the covering of his brain becomes soft,
phrases.notes: The "covering of his brain" means the skull.

phrases.english: and he opens it up to his brain
and brings four myrtle leaves

phrases.aramaic: וּמַדְלֵי כֹּל חַד כַּרְעָא וּמוֹתֵיב חַד,
phrases.english: and lifts one foot at a time and places one leaf under it,
phrases.notes: The גמרא never names it, but these are the feet of the creature sitting on the brain.

phrases.english: and takes it with tweezers and burns it.
For if not, it comes back onto him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָטֵיל לֵיהּ תְּלָת מְאָה כָּסֵי עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes אביי's treatment from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How ראתן is treated (asked in step 10).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soften and open the skull, lift the creature off the brain using myrtle leaves and tweezers, and burn it so it does not return.

steps.title: Sages who kept far away from people with ראתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן warns people to watch out for the flies on those with ראתן. רבי זירא, רבי אלעזר, רבי אמי and רבי אסי each kept their distance in their own way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן used to announce: Be careful of the flies on people with ראתן. רבי זירא would not sit where the wind blew from a sick person. רבי אלעזר would not go into a sick person's tent. רבי אמי and רבי אסי would not eat eggs from the alley where a sick person lived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how seriously the Sages treated ראתן as a disease that spreads. Each one guarded himself in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said flies rest on someone with ראתן, and now רבי יוחנן warns that those flies can spread it. The other Sages went further and avoided even the wind, the tent, and food from the sick person's alley. This sets up the contrast with רבי יהושע בן לוי in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: his wind, the air coming from him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan would announce:
Be careful of the flies of those with ra'atan.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא לָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּזִיקֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira would not sit in his wind.
phrases.notes: He means downwind of the sick person, where the air blows from him toward you.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar would not enter his tent.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי לָא הֲווֹ אָכְלִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi would not eat
eggs from that alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the treatment, the גמרא turns to how the Sages protected themselves from ראתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראתן spreads, so one should stay away from its flies, wind, tent, and even eggs from the sick person's alley.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי sits with the sick and learns
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the others, רבי יהושע בן לוי stayed close to people with ראתן and learned תורה. He reasoned from a פסוק that the תורה would protect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי would stay close to them and learn תורה. He said: The פסוק calls the תורה "a loving hind and a graceful doe." If it brings grace to those who learn it, won't it also protect them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite approach: one Sage did not keep away, because he relied on the protection of learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "יעלת חן" as if it said the תורה "brings up grace" on its learners. From that he reasons: if it gives grace, it surely shields them from harm too. This is why he could sit with the sick while the other Sages could not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step introduces רבי יהושע בן לוי's special closeness to the תורה, which leads straight into the story of his death.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִיכְרָךְ בְּהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would attach himself to them
and occupy himself with Torah. He said:
"A loving hind and a graceful doe"
phrases.notes: משלי 5:19

phrases.english: If it brings grace upon those who learn it,
phrases.notes: He reads יעלת as "brings up," like the word מעלה.

phrases.english: would it not protect them?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִיכְרָךְ בְּהוּ וְעָסֵיק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the Sages in step 13 who kept their distance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה protects a person, so רבי יהושע בן לוי could stay near people with ראתן.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי takes the knife and jumps into גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יהושע בן לוי was about to die, the מלאך המות was told to do what he wanted. He took the angel's knife, asked to see his place in גן עדן, and jumped in.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he was about to die, they told the מלאך המות: Go and do what he wishes. He went and appeared to him. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Show me my place. The angel said: All right. He said: Give me your knife, so you won't scare me on the way. The angel gave it to him. When they got there, the angel lifted him up and was showing him, and he jumped and fell over to the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells a story about how רבי יהושע בן לוי died, or rather did not die in the usual way. He cleverly gets into גן עדן alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he was so righteous, the angel was told to follow his wishes. He used that twice: first to take the knife the angel kills with, and then to be brought to the edge of גן עדן. Once he was lifted up to look, he jumped straight in.

phrases.english: When he was dying,
they said to the Angel of Death:
Go, do his wish for him.
He went and appeared to him.
He said to him: Show me my place.
He said to him: Very well.
He said to him: Give me your knife,
in case you frighten me on the way.
He gave it to him.
When he arrived there, he lifted him up,
and was showing it to him.
He jumped and fell to that other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה שָׁכֵיב, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְמַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with רבי יהושע בן לוי, now telling the story of the end of his life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of his righteousness, the מלאך המות had to follow his wishes, and he used this to enter גן עדן alive.

steps.title: The oath and ה׳'s decision
steps.stepSummary: The angel grabs his cloak, but רבי יהושע בן לוי swears he will not come. הקב"ה rules that he stays only if he never had an oath undone in his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angel grabbed him by the corner of his cloak. He said: I swear I am not coming. הקב"ה said: If he ever asked to have an oath undone, he must go back. If not, he does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The angel tries to pull him out, so רבי יהושע בן לוי makes an oath to stay. הקב"ה decides whether that oath holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is about his past: if he ever had an oath undone, he could undo this one too, so it would not hold. Since he never did, his oath stands and he stays in גן עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: asked to have an oath undone

phrases.english: He grabbed him by the corner of his cloak.
He said to him: I swear that I will not come.
The Holy One, blessed be He, said:
If he ever asked to undo an oath, he must return.
If not, he need not return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after he jumps into גן עדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His oath to stay holds because he never in his life had an oath undone.

steps.title: The knife is returned and אליהו announces his arrival
steps.stepSummary: He refuses to give back the knife until a בת קול tells him the world needs it. אליהו then announces: Make room for the son of Levi.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angel said: Give me my knife. He would not give it. A בת קול came out and told him: Give it to him, because the world's creatures need it. אליהו announced before him: Make room for the son of Levi! Make room for the son of Levi!
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The knife goes back to the angel, and רבי יהושע בן לוי is welcomed into גן עדן with honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wanted to keep the knife, it seems so that people would stop dying, but the בת קול says death is part of how the world works. אליהו's double announcement shows how great an honor he received.
steps.whatToRemember: The Sages kept away from ראתן, but רבי יהושע בן לוי trusted the תורה's protection, and the story shows how great his righteousness was: he entered גן עדן alive.

phrases.english: He said to him: Give me my knife.
He would not give it to him.
A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
Give it to him, for it is needed for the created beings.
phrases.notes: The knife is needed because people in the world have to die at their time.

phrases.english: Elijah announced before him:
Make room for the son of Levi!
Make room for the son of Levi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the story after הקב"ה lets him stay.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Death must stay in the world, so the knife goes back, and רבי יהושע בן לוי is welcomed into גן עדן with great honor.

steps.title: The rainbow question in גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי meets רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in גן עדן. He says a rainbow was seen in his days, so רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says he cannot be the famous son of Levi.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found רבי שמעון בן יוחאי sitting on thirteen golden stools. He asked: Are you the son of Levi? He said: Yes. Was a rainbow seen in your days? Yes. If so, you are not the son of Levi.
steps.whatsHappening: Now inside גן עדן, רבי יהושע בן לוי is tested by רבי שמעון בן יוחאי with a question about the rainbow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rainbow is a sign that the world deserves punishment. In the days of a truly great צדיק, his merit protects the world, so no rainbow should appear. When רבי יהושע בן לוי answers yes, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי concludes he is not that great a צדיק.

keyTerms.meaning: Rainbow, a sign that the world deserves punishment
The son of Levi, meaning רבי יהושע בן לוי

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
phrases.english: He went and found Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהושע בן לוי, who just jumped into גן עדן.

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב עַל תְּלָת עֲשַׂר תַּכְטָקֵי פִּיזָּא.
phrases.english: who was sitting on thirteen golden stools.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ הוּא בַּר לֵיוַאי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you the son of Levi?
He said to him: Yes.
Was a rainbow seen in your days?
He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, אִי אַתָּה בַּר לֵיוַאי.
phrases.english: If so, you are not the son of Levi.
phrases.notes: He means a truly great צדיק protects his generation, so no rainbow should be seen in his days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רבי יהושע בן לוי enters גן עדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rainbow in someone's lifetime shows he was not a complete צדיק whose merit protected the world.

steps.title: There really was no rainbow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that no rainbow was really seen in his days. He said yes only out of humility.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There was no rainbow at all. Rather, he thought: I will not take credit for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in to correct the impression from the story: רבי יהושע בן לוי was in fact that great.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conclusion that he was not a complete צדיק is rejected. His 'yes' was not true. He said it on purpose so he would not be praised for his own goodness.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not take credit for myself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבי יהושע בן לוי was less than a complete צדיק. The גמרא says outright that no rainbow appeared in his days.

phrases.english: But that is not so,
for there was nothing at all.
Rather, he thought:
I will not take credit for myself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn from his answer about the rainbow.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that he was not a complete צדיק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His 'yes' was humility, not the truth. No rainbow was ever seen.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בר פפא asks for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא, a friend of the מלאך המות, is about to die. He asks for thirty days to review his learning, and the angel agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא was his friend. When he was about to die, they told the מלאך המות: Go, do what he wants. He appeared to him. He said: Leave me thirty days to review my learning, for they say: Happy is one who comes here with his learning in his hand. He left him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new, similar story about another חכם and the מלאך המות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהושע בן לוי, רבי חנינא בר פפא is given his wish at death. His first wish is to arrive in the next world with his learning fresh, and the angel gives him the time.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא שׁוֹשְׁבִינֵיהּ הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa was his friend.
phrases.notes: "His" means the מלאך המות's friend.

phrases.english: When he was about to die,
they said to the Angel of Death:
Go, do for him what he wants.
He went to him and appeared to him.
He said to him: Leave me thirty days
until I review my learning.
For they say: Happy is one who comes here
with his learning in his hand.
He left him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא שׁוֹשְׁבִינֵיהּ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that closely matches the story of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is praiseworthy to arrive in the next world with one's learning fresh.

steps.title: He asks for the knife, and the angel sees through it
steps.stepSummary: After thirty days, רבי חנינא בר פפא asks to see his place and asks for the knife. The angel realizes he is copying רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: After thirty days he appeared to him again. He said: Show me my place. He said: Very well. He said: Give me your knife, so you don't frighten me on the way. He said: Do you want to do to me what your friend did?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא tries the same plan רבי יהושע בן לוי used, and the מלאך המות catches on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for the knife was the trick that let רבי יהושע בן לוי enter גן עדן alive. The angel refuses to be fooled a second time.

phrases.aramaic: לְבָתַר תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין אֲזַל אִיתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: After thirty days he went and appeared to him.
He said to him: Show me my place.
He said to him: Very well.
He said to him: Give me your knife,
lest you frighten me on the way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּחַבְרָךְ בָּעֵית לְמִיעְבַּד לִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you want to do to me like your friend did?
phrases.notes: The friend is רבי יהושע בן לוי, who took the knife and jumped into גן עדן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין אֲזַל אִיתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the thirty days run out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאך המות will not allow the trick of רבי יהושע בן לוי to be repeated.

steps.title: Did you sit with people who had ראתן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא claims he kept the whole תורה. The angel answers that he never did what made רבי יהושע בן לוי special.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Bring a ספר תורה and see if anything written in it was not kept by me. He said: Did you attach yourself to people with ראתן and learn תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא argues that he deserves the same reward, and the angel turns down his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping the whole תורה is not enough to be equal to רבי יהושע בן לוי. What set him apart was his brave closeness to people with ראתן while learning תורה, from step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: People sick with ראתן, a dangerous disease

phrases.english: He said to him: Bring a Torah scroll
and see whether there is anything
written in it that I have not fulfilled.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי אִיכָּרַכְתְּ בְּבַעֲלֵי רָאתָן
phrases.english: He said to him: Did you attach yourself to those with ra'atan
and occupy yourself with Torah?
phrases.notes: This points back to what רבי יהושע בן לוי did (step 14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חנינא בר פפא defends his request, and the angel rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי חנינא בר פפא's claim that he equals רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He never stayed close to people with ראתן while learning תורה.

steps.title: A pillar of fire at his death
steps.stepSummary: Even though he was not equal to רבי יהושע בן לוי, a pillar of fire separated רבי חנינא בר פפא from everyone at his death. This happens to only one or two people in a generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, when he died, a pillar of fire separated him from the world. We have a tradition that this happens only for one or two in a generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רבי חנינא בר פפא was still extremely great, and proves it with the pillar of fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angel's refusal does not mean he was ordinary. The rare pillar of fire shows he was among the top one or two people of his generation.

phrases.english: And even so,
when he passed away,
a pillar of fire separated him
between himself and the world.
And we have a tradition that a pillar of fire does not separate

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְחַד בְּדָרָא אוֹ לִתְרֵין בְּדָרָא.
phrases.english: except for one in a generation or two in a generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Balances the angel's refusal by showing how great רבי חנינא בר פפא still was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pillar of fire at death marks one of the one or two greatest people in a generation.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי gets the pillar to leave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי asks the pillar to go away for the honor of the חכמים, then for the father's honor. It goes away only when he asks for the sake of רבי חנינא בר פפא's own honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי came near and said: Do it for the honor of the חכמים. No response. Do it for your father's honor. No response. Do it for your own honor. It went away.
steps.whatsHappening: The pillar of fire blocks people from caring for the body, so רבי אלכסנדרי asks it to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the third request works. Leaving the body unburied would be a disgrace to רבי חנינא בר פפא himself, so it is his own honor that moves the pillar.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri approached him,
and said: "Do it for the honor of the Sages."
phrases.notes: He is asking for the pillar to move away so they can bury him.

phrases.english: He paid no attention.
"Do it for the honor of your father."
He paid no attention.
"Do it for your own honor,"
and it went away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how the pillar of fire was finally removed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pillar left only when asked for the sake of the deceased's own honor.

steps.title: אביי explains the purpose of the pillar
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the pillar of fire was there to separate רבי חנינא בר פפא from people who had not kept the תורה completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The pillar was to separate him from someone who did not keep even one letter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the pillar of fire was needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בר פפא had kept everything in the תורה. The pillar kept him apart from people who were not on his level, even those who missed only a small part.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
To exclude him from one who did not fulfill
(even one letter).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמַּאן דְּלָא קַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of the pillar of fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pillar separated the one who kept the whole תורה from those who did not.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנא jabs at אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא answers that the pillar was there to separate him from אביי himself, who had no railing on his roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said to him: To separate him from you, Master, who has no railing on his roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנא uses אביי's own words to sharply point out a מצוה אביי seemed to be missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a מעקה on a roof is a מצוה. If אביי had none, then אביי himself was one of the people who did not keep everything.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Master, a polite way of saying 'you'
A safety railing around a roof

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Matna said to him:
To exclude him from the Master,
who does not have a railing on his roof.
phrases.notes: דברים 22:8

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns אביי's explanation into a criticism of אביי himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's own behavior, using his own explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the pillar separates those who missed a מצוה, then אביי, with no מעקה, is one of them.

steps.title: The railing had just blown down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends אביי. He did have a railing, but the wind had knocked it down at that very time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There was a railing, and at that time the wind had knocked it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in to clear אביי's name and close the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר מתנא's criticism is rejected. אביי had kept the מצוה of מעקה, and the missing railing was only a recent accident.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי was a complete צדיק, and his humble answer about the rainbow was not true. רבי חנינא בר פפא could not copy his entry into גן עדן, yet he was so great that a rare pillar of fire marked his death. The גמרא also defends אביי's keeping of the מצוה of מעקה.

phrases.english: But that is not so:
there was one,
and it was just at that time that the wind had blown it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר מתנא's criticism of אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that אביי had no מעקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He did have one. The wind had just knocked it down.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי kept the מצוה of מעקה, and the missing railing was only a passing accident.

steps.title: Why there is no ראתן in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says people in בבל do not get רָאתָן because they eat beets and drink beer made from הִיזְמֵי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Why are there no people with רָאתָן in בבל? Because they eat beets and drink beer made from the הִיזְמֵי plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רָאתָן, the skin disease discussed before the story. רבי חנינא explains why it is not found in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא described how dangerous רָאתָן is. Now רבי חנינא adds new information: the local diet in בבל protects people from it. Beets and הִיזְמֵי beer act like a natural protection.

keyTerms.meaning: People who suffer from רָאתָן, a serious skin disease
A kind of plant that beer was made from

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is going back to רָאתָן from earlier in the sugya, after the story about רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין בַּעֲלֵי רָאתָן בְּבָבֶל —
phrases.english: For what reason are there no people with ra'atan in Babylonia?
phrases.notes: רָאתָן is the dangerous skin disease the גמרא talked about earlier on this daf.

phrases.english: Because they eat beets,
and drink beer made from hizmei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין בַּעֲלֵי רָאתָן בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends with step 27, the גמרא goes back to the earlier topic of רָאתָן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People in בבל do not get רָאתָן because of their diet of beets and הִיזְמֵי beer.

steps.title: Why there is no צרעת in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says people in בבל do not get צרעת because they eat beets, drink beer, and bathe in the פרת river.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why are there no people with צרעת in בבל? Because they eat beets, drink beer, and bathe in the waters of the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a similar statement about a different skin disease, צרעת. He gives a similar reason with one thing added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's statement is built just like רבי חנינא's. He keeps beets and beer, and adds a third reason: bathing in the waters of the פרת. All three were seen as healthy for the body.

keyTerms.meaning: People with צרעת, a skin disease

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
For what reason are there no lepers in Babylonia?
Because they eat beets,
and drink beer,
and bathe in the waters of the Euphrates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מְצוֹרָעִין בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A similar statement to step 28, about צרעת instead of רָאתָן, with one more reason added.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People in בבל do not get צרעת because of beets, beer, and bathing in the פרת.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the perek הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.stepSummary: The perek הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ ends with the הדרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the perek. It is not part of the argument. It marks that the chapter is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן says we hope to come back and learn this perek again. The perek is named after its first words, הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, about a husband who makes a vow that forbids his wife from benefiting from him.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing words said at the end of a perek
One who makes a vow affecting his wife, the name of this perek

steps.whatToRemember: The perek ends with aggadic statements about health in בבל, after the earlier discussion of the skin diseases that can force a husband to divorce.

phrases.english: May we return to you
[chapter] "One who vows that his wife"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole perek after the final aggadic statements.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ is complete.
